title: No release from wrath until sin is retracted by serious repentance joined to faith
source_text: VI. Nemo enim propter Christi mortem & passionem cessat obnoxius esse irae divinae, quam peccata ejus provocarunt, quin prius peccata sua retractaverit ac deseruerit per seriam poenitentiam, cui juncta sit fides, per quam ad Dei misericordiam in Christo confugiat. Quippe haec est lex ab aeterno a Deo constituta, ut quicunque in peccato perseverat ad poenas peccato debitas maneat obligatus: ab illa vero obligatione immunis fiat peccator statim atque peccato renunciat, & corde contrito quaerit & implorat Dei gratiam & misericordiam.
pass_a_gloss: For no one, on account of Christ’s death and passion, ceases to be liable to the divine wrath which his sins provoked, unless he has first retracted and deserted his sins through serious repentance, to which faith is joined, through which he flees to God’s mercy in Christ. For this is the law constituted by God from eternity, that whoever perseveres in sin remains bound to the penalties owed to sin: but the sinner becomes immune from that obligation as soon as he renounces sin and with a contrite heart seeks and implores God’s grace and mercy.
pass_b_english: Christ’s death frees no one from provoked wrath while he still perseveres in sin.
Eternal law: renounce sin with contrite faith-seeking, and the penalty-obligation lifts.

choices.why: Obligation ceases at renunciation + contrite seeking.
